what.text: This page follows refugees from Syria living in Türkiye.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 2347756 Syrian refugees in Türkiye, the largest group of Syrian refugees in any single country.
Germany, Lebanon and Jordan are the next largest hosts.

why.text: Protests from March 2011 turned into armed conflict, which UCDP records at war level from 2011 between the government and Syrian insurgents.
UCDP also records armed conflict with the Islamic State group in Syria from 2013 to 2025.

when.text: The number of Syrian refugees in Türkiye peaked at 3737369 in 2021 and was lower by the end of 2025.
Türkiye set out temporary protection for Syrians in a regulation on 22 October 2014, and the EU–Türkiye statement followed on 18 March 2016.
After the government of Bashar al-Assad fell on 8 December 2024, returns from Türkiye to Syria rose in UNHCR's returns data.

how.text: Türkiye registers Syrians under temporary protection rather than full refugee status, and UNHCR reports them as refugees.
The figures count registered people only.
Large earthquakes struck south-eastern Türkiye and northern Syria on 6 February 2023, where many Syrian refugees live; IDMC counts that displacement in a separate series.
